topic_summary: Analysis of the abortion debate as a contested kernel where different parties read the personhood-boundary commitment differently. The conception reading, viability reading, and birth reading each instantiate structurally different constraints with distinct victim sets, beneficiary structures, and authority groundings. This is not a disagreement about observer position relative to one constraint, but about which constraint exists to be observed.

key_entities: Fetus/embryo (entity whose moral status is contested)
Pregnant person (rights-holder in all readings, scope varies)
State authority (enforcement mechanism for whichever reading prevails)
Religious institutions (natural-law authority grounding for conception reading)
Autonomy framework (liberal rights grounding for birth reading)
key_tensions: Fetal moral status vs maternal autonomy (structural opposition in all readings)
Natural law vs positive law (authority grounding collision)
Biological continuity vs legal/social personhood (ontological vs constructed status)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The personhood-boundary kernel: a shared commitment that moral status begins at some point in human development, but contested as to when
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Multiple competing authorities: religious natural-law traditions, medical profession (viability), legal positivism (birth), feminist autonomy frameworks

readings.commitment: Moral status begins at conception; the zygote is a rights-bearing person
readings.authority_grounding: Natural law / religious doctrine (Catholic, evangelical Protestant traditions)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus enters victim set at conception; abortion becomes homicide-equivalent; high suppression of alternative readings; state becomes enforcer of fetal rights against maternal autonomy

readings.commitment: Moral status begins at viability (capacity for independent life outside womb)
readings.authority_grounding: Medical profession / Roe v. Wade framework (trimester compromise)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus enters victim set at ~24 weeks; pre-viability abortion permitted; post-viability restricted; state balances competing interests rather than enforcing absolute fetal rights

readings.commitment: Moral status begins at birth; the fetus is not a rights-bearing person
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus not in victim set; pregnant person is sole rights-holder; abortion is healthcare decision; no state enforcement of fetal interests

axes.structural_delta: Fetus as rights-bearing person from conception; abortion as homicide-equivalent
axes.primary_observable: Legal status of abortion (criminal vs permitted); enforcement mechanisms (prosecution rates, clinic restrictions)
axes.selection_reason: First reading: highest extractiveness; clearest victim set; natural-law authority grounding

axes.structural_delta: Fetus as potential person at viability; state balances competing interests
axes.primary_observable: Trimester framework enforcement; viability determination protocols; gestational limits in law
axes.selection_reason: Second reading: moderate extractiveness; distinct authority structure (medical profession); compromise position

axes.structural_delta: Pregnant person as sole rights-holder; fetus not in victim set
axes.primary_observable: Abortion access rates; legal status (healthcare vs crime); state non-interference
axes.selection_reason: Third reading: lowest extractiveness; autonomy-grounding; fetus outside victim set

omegas.description: Historical quickening reading (fetal movement as personhood marker) not analyzed. Pre-modern authority structure; largely displaced by medical/legal frameworks but may resurface in traditionalist contexts.

Gradualist reading (moral status increases continuously from conception to birth) not analyzed. Would emit variable victim set and epsilon over time; structurally distinct from discrete-boundary readings.
Conception reading enforcement targets pregnant persons and providers, not male partners. Beneficiary structure may include patriarchal control mechanisms beyond religious authority.
Medical technology shifts viability earlier over time. Viability reading's epsilon may increase as the window of permitted abortion narrows, potentially collapsing toward conception reading.
omegas.source: F03 (Hasty Generalization) + commitment system drift analysis

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: viability_reading classified as tangled_rope but medical technology drift may reclassify it as scaffold (temporary compromise collapsing under technological pressure). Generated omega_viability_drift to bound this uncertainty. Kernel structure confirmed: three readings emit genuinely different constraints with distinct victim sets and authority groundings.
